notes: A 97 MB proof against a 200-byte contract. The 237 bytes are cases/test87/request.json: the two claim records (118 B each) carrying only reverse, input_integers, output_integers, objective (NonIncreasing forward, Equal reverse), an empty projection array and a null inverse; it is byte-identical to the RPA preamble's claims array (tools/prepare_test87.py:188). It is small because it names nothing model-scale: the operands are the models supplied separately (source.mcm 11,221,455 B, target.mcm 3,435,753 B) and the claim quantifies over every integer point of that pair, so 63,009 variables and 507 rows cost zero contract bytes. The proof cannot be equally small because the kernel is a checker with no derivation primitive for this reduction: blocks[0] is 97,411,412 B (96.0%) of pure witness data - 16,355 IntervalWitness records with per-member lower/upper Exprs and checks, 59,019 Cases branches (one per merged coordinate), 1,020 Round steps, 91,729 generated rows, 61,467 obligations - and even the easy reverse direction must satisfy the complete-Return contract (one affine expression per output coordinate, one check per obligation, no surplus): 63,009 map entries of which 42,667 are literal zeros, 189,535 obligations, 4,049,607 B. Size is Theta(#merged coordinates + #rows x support), not O(1); shrinking it needs build-time rules (RULE_BUILDERS) or a batch encoding (BATCH_TEMPLATES), not a smaller claim.
